Research

My work asks how geometric constraints, such as bounded curvature or a minimum thickness, shape the topology and the optimal configurations of curves, ribbons and disk systems.

Current programme

Variational rigidity and contact strata

A unified variational method for disk diagrams, finite packing problems and perimeter minimisation under geometric constraints. Configurations are stratified by their contact graphs (which disks touch), and the admissible deformations at each stratum are governed by the active contacts.

First- and second-order variational analysis on these strata gives a systematic way to decide when a configuration is rigid, when it can flex, and when it is minimal.

Related papers

  • Intrinsic Geometry of Hard Disk Clusters (2026)

Current programme

Critical ribbon loops and Gordian unknots

Ribbons of fixed width and curvature bound can be topologically trivial and still be geometrically locked. The Gordian unknot conjecture asserts that such geometrically distinct unknots exist, and that they cannot be untied through constrained deformations.

The same ideas extend to links, where one studies Gordian unlinks and the geometric constraints that obstruct link isotopy.

Related papers

  • Geometric Constraints in Link Isotopy (2025)
  • Gordian Unlinks (2025)
  • Thin Gordian Unlinks (2023)
  • Immersed flat ribbon knots (2020)

Doctoral work

Bounded curvature paths

A bounded curvature path is a $C^1$ and piecewise $C^2$ path in a manifold $M$ joining two elements of the tangent bundle $TM$, with curvature bounded by a positive constant. In 1961 Lester Dubins raised the question of the homotopy classes of such paths in the plane; my doctoral dissertation closes the programme he proposed.

Let $\Gamma(n)$ be the space of bounded curvature paths with fixed endpoints in $T\mathbb{R}^2$ and winding number $n$. Four proximity conditions on the endpoints give qualitative insight into the topology of $\Gamma(n)$, for instance the number of homotopy classes it contains.

The shortest elements of $\Gamma(n)$ are classified for every $n$ and every pair of endpoints, recovering the CSC and CCC characterisation of Dubins (1957). A continuity argument ensures the curvature bound is never violated during a deformation, which yields the classification of homotopy classes, including classes made exclusively of embedded paths.

Related papers

  • A geometric approach to shortest bounded curvature paths (2014)
  • Length minimising bounded curvature paths in homotopy classes (2014)
  • Non-uniqueness of the homotopy class of bounded curvature paths (2014)
  • The classification of homotopy classes of bounded curvature paths (2014)
